This project was a travel-style promotional poster designed for the Mercedes-Benz Classic Center to celebrate their move to Long Beach, CA and spotlight one of their restored vehicles, the G55 Cabrio. The goal was to create a printed 12 x 18 inch poster in CMYK that blended brand heritage with a sense of adventure, using a U.S. travel destination to frame the story visually. Hawaii’s volcanic landscape became the setting, pairing naturally with the rugged character of the G-Class. The poster needed to both inform viewers of the center’s new location and capture attention with a bold, aspirational image rooted in Mercedes-Benz’s identity.

The design required synthesizing a huge amount of research into one cohesive visual. I explored the Classic Center’s audience, Mercedes-Benz heritage, state-specific visuals, Art Deco references, vintage automotive posters, and the engineering history of the G55 Cabrio. Narrowing these ideas into something focused and intentional took time and thoughtful iteration. The piece needed to feel adventurous and modern without losing the elegance and prestige of the brand. Finding that middle ground, professional but bold, classic but energetic, became the central creative challenge.

I pulled from classic travel posters, Art Deco influences, and the engineering story behind the G-Class. Hawaii’s volcanic textures, color palette, and iconic rainbow imagery shaped the direction. Understanding the Classic Center’s audience and the G55 Cabrio’s personality helped determine the tone: adventurous, nostalgic, and premium.

The poster centers the bright yellow G55 Cabrio against a dramatic volcanic backdrop, with the tagline “Reaching new heights” to frame the story. The composition mixes travel poster energy with Mercedes-Benz elegance using period type, vintage branding marks, and a bold, simplified landscape. The result is a clean, eye-catching piece that promotes the Classic Center while giving the car its moment.
